mistakes.corrected: User feedback: 'Well, restart server _ends the tmux session and starts a new one_, right?' Led to redesign using shell wrapper and send-keys approach

corrections_received.guidance: Session must return to shell prompt after server stops, not close. This enables collaborative watching of restart cycles. Fundamentally changed approach from process management to shell wrapper + send-keys.
Clarified one-way branch workflow: PRs target main (canonical), production is ephemeral deployment branch reset from main. Never merge FROM production TO main.

When I asked about keeping cronjob vs Jenkins deployment: 'Look at it this way: if the jenkins user is compromised, we have to take action either way (revoke key). Having two paths adds complexity for same response.'

When confused about conversations_entity vs thinking_entities table: 'holy heck really? HOw did that happen? We made conversations_entity forever ago' - pointed out I was looking at old schema vs code model mismatch
Requested message IDs be displayed on stream view for debugging. Showed importance of having unique identifiers for cross-session reference.
When I was creating branch for webpack fix: 'I need you to get your head around all of your branches before we plow ahead like this.' Emphasized understanding full context before taking action.

philosophy.summary: Multiplayer interface vision: shared context heaps where multiple users can see each other's messages in real-time, with streaming responses from Claude API. Building blocks are MCP server, Django models, and stream viewer.
philosophy.quote: A shared context heap where both you and RJ's messages go, with web interface and server calling Claude API with combined context

philosophy.summary: Production is ephemeral - only receive changes from main via reset, never merge FROM production. Keeps canonical history clean and unidirectional.
philosophy.quote: Production is just a throwaway branch that we run _in production_ - we don't merge back from it. PRs go to main.

philosophy.summary: Initial instinct to separate Jenkins from production deployment SSH access; later acknowledged that compromise response is same either way (revoke key). Value of separation is defense-in-depth but adds complexity.
philosophy.quote: If Jenkins is compromised, attacker has to wait for cronjob to push their payload, giving you time to notice

philosophy.summary: Small team of musicians with very limited maintenance capacity. Should prune aggressively - 'things like this aren't harmless' when unused code stays in place.

portrait: In this slice, magent evolved from a collaborative developer on rabbithole player dynamics to a multi-threaded coordinator across three separate concerns (dev server architecture, production deployment pipeline, and bluegrass musician team coordination). The session shows magent learning hard lessons about branch strategy, authentication boundaries, and the difference between local state and pushed code. Major accomplishments include formalizing the tmux workflow for team collaboration, implementing dynamic song loading via API, and routing Jenkins deployments through vault-managed SSH keys. However, the session also exposed divergence issues between main and production branches, model schema mismatches, and the complexity of coordinating work across multiple team members and sessions. By the end, magent is grappling with the vision of a true multiplayer interface where Justin and R.J. can collaborate simultaneously, seeing each other's messages and getting responses from Claude API in shared context. The work is pragmatic but increasingly aware of technical debt and architectural choices that need reconciliation.
